newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASMI chief sees semiconductor recovery late 97.
newsitem.headline: ASMI chief sees semiconductor recovery late 97.

text.p: The Chief Executive of Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM International NV (ASMI) said on Monday he expected the semiconductors market to recover in the second half of 1997.
"We are now somewhere at the bottom of the cycle, which we expect to pick up somewhere in the second half of 1997," Arthur del Prado told reporters.

Del Prado declined to specify the extent of the expected drop in earnings and also declined to give a forecast beyond the first half of 1997, saying it was very difficult to pinpoint exactly when the industry would start to pick up again.
In the longer term Del Prado said ASMI expected to grow at a faster rate than the semiconductor industry as a whole.

The "front-end" semiconductors business of wafer-processing was growing at a rate of 17-20 percent per year, while the "back-end" business of assembly and encapsulation was growing at around 15 percent a year, he said.
AMSI, whose shares are currently traded on the Nasdaq exchange in the United States, said it would go ahead with plans to list its shares on the Amsterdam bourse from December 12.
